classification.difficultyReason: Transfer the immediately preceding triangle-pair procedure to twelve points, including division by two, three consecutive partitions and subtraction.

content.prompt: Twelve points are arranged in order around a circle.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How many triangles can be drawn with these points as vertices?

answer.worked:
Choose three vertices from twelve points.
$$\begin{aligned}N&={}^{12}C_3\\&=220\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: In how many pairs of such triangles are the vertices of the two triangles distinct?

answer.worked:
Choose six vertices, then split them into two groups of three. Divide by $2$ because the pair is unordered.
$$\begin{aligned}N&={}^{12}C_6\times\frac{{}^{6}C_3}{2}\\&=924\times10\\&=9240\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: In how many such pairs will the triangles not overlap?

answer.worked:
Each selection of six vertices has three unordered partitions into consecutive triples in its circular order.
$$\begin{aligned}N&={}^{12}C_6\times3\\&=924\times3\\&=2772\end{aligned}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: In how many such pairs will the triangles overlap?

answer.worked:
Subtract the non-overlapping pairs from all pairs with distinct vertices.
$$\begin{aligned}N&=9240-2772\\&=6468\end{aligned}$$
